ingles.titulo: Did You Know the Azov Sea Is the Shallowest Sea on Earth?
ingles.descripcion: The Azov Sea reaches a maximum depth of only 14 meters, making it the shallowest sea in the world. Located between Russia and Ukraine, it connects to the Black Sea via the 4‑km‑wide Kerch Strait and serves as a key route for the Volga‑Don Canal. Its name comes from the Kipchak Turkic word “asak/azaq” meaning “lowlands,” and a Russian legend links it to the Cuman prince Azum.
